cards.explanation: The answer is that they proclaim the resurrection in Jesus. The text says the leaders were “…greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.” (Acts 4:2) So the message was the trouble, friends, and it brought the priests, the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees right up to Peter and John.
The answer is five thousand, friends! The text says “…the number of men grew to about five thousand.” (Acts 4:4) It also says many who heard the message believed. That's a whole lot of believers.

The answer is that they ask by what power or name Peter and John did it. The leaders question them: “By what power or what name did you do this?” (Acts 4:7) They want to know who is behind the healing. I think Peter was glad they asked, because he had a very good answer.

The answer is Jesus Christ of Nazareth, friends. Peter says, “It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed.” (Acts 4:10) He's not hiding the name or mumbling it. He says it plainly, in front of the very leaders who asked.

The answer is False. Peter says Jesus is the one “…whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead…” (Acts 4:10) He puts it straight to the council and doesn't tiptoe around it, friends. And he doesn't stop at the crucifixion, because God raised Jesus up.

The answer is the rulers and elders in that room. Peter is talking to “Rulers and elders of the people!” (Acts 4:8) and then says Jesus is “the stone you builders rejected…” (Acts 4:11) He says “you,” and the rulers and elders are the ones he's speaking to. Peter's not shy, friends, that's for sure.

The word is name. Peter says, “Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.” (Acts 4:12) He's already been talking about the name of Jesus, and now he says it's the only one. That's a big statement, friends, from a man who was in custody the night before.

The answer is Jesus, friends. The council saw their boldness and realized they were unschooled, ordinary men, and “…they marveled and took note that these men had been with Jesus.” (Acts 4:13) The text doesn't say it was anything else they noticed. Being around Jesus leaves a mark.

The answer is True. The text says that “…seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say in response.” (Acts 4:14) The healed man was right there with them, friends. That's the kind of moment where you open your mouth and nothing comes out.

The answer is that they warn them not to speak in this name. The council says, “…to keep this message from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name.” (Acts 4:17) They can't deny the miracle, friends, so they go after the message instead.

The answer is speaking about what they saw and heard. Peter and John say, “For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.” (Acts 4:20) They saw it and heard it, and they can't keep it in. I couldn't keep quiet about a fresh batch of cookies, either, friends.

The word is glorifying, friends! The text says, “They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were glorifying God for what had happened.” (Acts 4:21) The whole crowd was praising God. The council had a problem, and the crowd was the reason.

The answer is True. The text says, “When the believers heard this, they lifted up their voices to God with one accord.” (Acts 4:24) They lifted their voices together, friends. The report came from Peter and John, who had returned to their own people (Acts 4:23).

The answer is the Lord and His Anointed One. The believers quote David, “The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against His Anointed One.” (Acts 4:26) So the gathering is against the Lord Himself and His Anointed One, friends.

The answer is what God had decided beforehand. The believers pray, “They carried out what Your hand and will had decided beforehand would happen.” (Acts 4:28) Herod and Pilate were plotting, friends, but what they ended up carrying out is what God's hand and will had decided beforehand. The believers say it right in their prayer.

The answer is boldness to speak His word, friends. They pray, “…enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness…” (Acts 4:29) They'd just brought the council's threats before God, and they asked for complete boldness. I'd have asked for a different problem.
The word is shaken, friends! The text says, “After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken…” (Acts 4:31) The place was shaken after the prayer. That's one memorable prayer meeting.

The answer is False. The text says “…they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.” (Acts 4:31) They had just asked for boldness, friends, and the text says they spoke boldly. The same council that threatened them had no say in that.
